title: Hide AI images in image search
summary: DuckDuckGo has a real switch that filters generated pictures out of image results.
changes: Image results show far fewer generated pictures. It is a filter, not a guarantee — some slip through.

action.label: Search images without AI
action.placeholder: A photograph you are looking for

how: DuckDuckGo uses open, community-maintained blocklists of domains that mostly host generated imagery, and removes results from them. Opening the noai address switches every AI feature off at once, including this filter.
steps: Open the dropdown above the results marked "AI images".
Choose "Hide". The choice is remembered in that browser.
caveats: The filter works on where an image is hosted, not on the image itself, so it cannot catch everything.
The preference is stored in your browser and is lost if you clear site data.

sources.title: How to filter out AI images in DuckDuckGo search results (official)

title: Show photographs only
summary: Bing can restrict image results to photographs, which removes most generated art in one step.
changes: Illustrations, clip art, line drawings and most generated imagery disappear. Only photographs remain.
how: Bing classifies images by type. Asking for the photograph type excludes the illustration and drawing categories where most generated work is filed.
caveats: Photorealistic generated images are still classed as photographs and will appear.
Bing also offers a Licence filter, which pairs well with this.

sources.title: How to filter AI images from search results

title: Fewer generated pictures on Google Images
summary: Google has no filter, so exclude the words that generated images are usually tagged with.
changes: Results lose pages that mention the common generator names. It thins the flood; it does not stop it.

action.label: Search images, minus the obvious
action.placeholder: A photograph you are looking for

how: udm=2 is Google's own Images view. The minus terms remove pages whose text names the usual generators, which is how a great deal of generated imagery is labelled by the sites that host it.
caveats: Only as good as the labelling. Unlabelled generated images sail straight through.
It will also remove legitimate pages that happen to discuss AI.
Adding before:2023 to the query is a blunter but often more effective filter.

sources.title: How to filter AI images and content from Google search results

title: Blur out AI images everywhere
summary: An add-on that detects and hides generated images across search engines and social sites.
changes: Suspected generated images are hidden or blurred as pages load, on Google, Bing, DuckDuckGo, Pinterest and others.
how: The add-on combines domain blocklists with image analysis, so it catches some images that a domain list alone would miss.
caveats: Detection of generated imagery is imperfect by nature. Expect both misses and false alarms.
Desktop browsers only.
It inspects images on pages you visit; read its privacy statement before installing.

title: Look at art made by people
summary: A portfolio community for artists that does not permit generated work.
changes: Everything you see is presented as human-made, and the rule is enforced by the platform and its members.
how: Cara was founded in direct response to generated work flooding portfolio sites. Generated images are against its rules and it applies detection alongside human moderation.
caveats: Best for illustration, concept art and design rather than documentary photography.
Smaller than the big platforms, which is rather the point.

title: Free photographs taken by photographers
summary: Large libraries of real photographs with clear licensing and a named person behind each one.
changes: Every result has an author, a camera and a licence. You can use them, with attribution, without wondering where they came from.
how: These libraries index openly-licensed work from museums, archives, government agencies and individual photographers. Provenance is part of the record rather than an afterthought.
caveats: Generated images do appear in large user-upload libraries. Check the author's other work if it matters.
Flickr asks uploaders to tag AI-generated work; enforcement is imperfect.

title: Stock photography without the generated shelf
summary: The big free-photo sites now carry generated work. Here is how to see past it.
changes: You still get high-quality photographs, with the generated material filtered or avoided.

alternatives.label: Public domain archives at Flickr Commons

how: Most large libraries now require uploaders to label generated content, and many surface a filter. The labels are the thing to look for on the image page before you use it.
caveats: Labelling is self-declared and inconsistent.
If provenance genuinely matters — journalism, history, evidence — use an archive or a named photographer's own site instead.

title: Check whether a picture is real
summary: Before you believe or share an image, find out where else it has appeared.
changes: You see the earliest and most credible places the image has been published, which usually settles the question.
how: A generated image has no history. A real photograph almost always does — a news agency, a photographer's portfolio, an older post. TinEye sorts by oldest first, which is exactly what you want.
steps: Upload it to TinEye and sort results by "Oldest".
No history at all, or a first appearance on a content farm, is a strong signal.
caveats: Automatic AI-detection tools are unreliable in both directions. Provenance is better evidence than a detector's score.
Cropped or re-compressed images are harder to trace.

title: See fewer generated pins
summary: Pinterest added controls to reduce generated imagery in the categories where it bothers people most.
changes: Your home feed shows fewer generated pins in the categories you adjust. Labels appear on pins Pinterest believes were generated.
steps: Open Pinterest settings while signed in.
Look under Privacy and data, or the "Refine your recommendations" controls.
Reduce generated content for the categories offered — beauty, art, fashion and home decor were the first supported.
On individual pins, use the three-dot menu → "See less like this".
caveats: The control is applied per category rather than everywhere, and coverage varies by region.
It reduces rather than removes.

title: Commission a person instead
summary: If you need an image made, hiring an illustrator is often quicker and cheaper than people assume.
changes: You get something made for your purpose, with rights you can actually rely on, by someone who will answer your questions.
how: Portfolio sites are searchable by style and medium, and most artists publish their commission terms and rates openly.
caveats: Behance and ArtStation both host generated work; both now label it and allow you to filter. Check the artist's process posts.
Agree licence and usage in writing before work begins.
